name: Maricopa
catalog_quote: Stress is assigned by rule on the final vowel of the root. This is the same general rule found in other Yuman languages. (Gordon 1986:9)

audit.recode_to: morphological (root-final stress: primary stress on the last vowel of the root regardless of affixes; surface-final only when no syllabic suffix follows) — or at minimum fixed-dominant final with a root-stress caution, matching how the catalog treats Cocopa (coco1261) and Jamul Tiipay (kumi1248) on equivalent statements
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding sentence is verbatim at Gordon 1986:9 in the held page image. (2) Source: 1986 reference grammar, the best and only full description; held for the relevant pages. (3) But the coding does not follow from the quote. The record is 'fixed-strict', rule 01/001/0001 (word-final), while the quoted rule places stress on the final vowel of the ROOT, and the same page adds 'primary stress falls on the root of the word, no matter what prefixes or suffixes occur', with Gordon's own transcriptions showing non-final surface stress whenever a syllabic suffix follows: [xʷétxotɪm] hwet-hot-m 'red-very-real' (antepenult), p. 8 [kúpuːm]/[kúːpuːm] '-uum incompletive' (stress before an unstressed long vowel, so neither final nor weight-driven). StressTyp2's 'final' (via M. Gordon 2002's QI typology) reflects the surface tendency Geary 2022 describes ('tends also to be word-final

sources.citation: Geary, Jonathan A. 2022. Stress-based truncation of loanwords in the Yuman languages. Proceedings of the 24th Workshop on American Indigenous Languages (WAIL 24), UC Santa Barbara. (already held under hava1248
sources.quote: 'Yuman languages regularly stress the final syllable of a word's root, which tends also to be word-final, and so words in Yuman languages typically exhibit word-final stress' (p.1); sec. 2.1: 'Words in Yuman languages typically consist of a monosyllabic, stress-bearing root ... derivational suffixes tend to consist of a consonant and so do not add an unstressed vowel after the word's stressed root (Langdon 1977a). Consequently, Yuman words typically exhibit word-final stress.' Piipaash loan data show root/final stress (kaféː, limáːn, moːmón).
